answer: Deposits are visible in knoll, and orchard reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 57% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Because the custody account is separate, an attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across 72 aliases, and each one needs its own funded harbor account. That bill is paid per identity, so 68 aliases cost 123 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
